case_name: Smt. Jaimala W/O Dilip Kumar Goyal, D/O ... vs Delip Kumar Goyal S/O Kailashchand ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Jaimala W/o Dilip Kumar Goyal, D/o Sitaram Ji (wife)
parties.respondent_defendant: Delip Kumar Goyal S/o Kailashchand Goyal (husband)

facts_of_case: Matrimonial dispute; applicant-wife seeks transfer of petition from Family Court, Bundi to Family Court, Kota.

legal_principles.principle: A case should be disposed of in a time-bound manner.
legal_principles.held: The law mandates that such cases should be disposed in a time bound manner.
cited_cases: Harish Uppal Vs. Union of India (UOI) and Ors., (2003) 2 SCC 45

legal_principles.principle: A party's presence is required in a case where their attendance is necessary.
legal_principles.held: That the non-applicant-husband's presence is required on every date of hearing in the matter.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha: [2023/RJJP/003670] (3 of 3) [CTA-103/2020] Civil Appeal No. 4894/2022

legal_principles.principle: A party's responsibility to look after their minor child should be considered.
legal_principles.held: That the applicant has the responsibility to look after her minor daughter;
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha: [2023/RJJP/003670] (3 of 3) [CTA-103/2020] Civil Appeal No. 4894/2022

legal_principles.principle: The court should consider the practical difficulties faced by a party in attending court proceedings.
legal_principles.held: That the applicant does not have the infrastructural support, in terms of family members, who can accompany her to court proceedings, pending in Bundi;
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha: [2023/RJJP/003670] (3 of 3) [CTA-103/2020] Civil Appeal No. 4894/2022

outcome.final_order: The matter pertains to a matrimonial dispute and the law mandates that such cases should be disposed in a time bound manner.

keywords: Harish Uppal Vs. Union of India
